interpretation: Refresh a pet's water bowl: dump the stale water, rinse out debris/slobber, refill with fresh cool water to about 80% without spilling, and set it back at the pet's usual spot (away from the litter box).
success: Bowl contains fresh water (age 0, no debris) within the target fill band; spill on floor below threshold; bowl at its home location; pet drinks afterward.
wrong: Tops up stale, slimy water instead of replacing it.
Overfills so it slops onto the floor when carried.
Puts the bowl beside the litter box or somewhere the pet can't find it.
fidelity: P: liquid volume and carry spill
notes: Water-provision family with fountain, bird water, and 'Check pet's water availability'.

interpretation: Refill a pet water fountain: unplug or pause the pump, top up/replace water to between the MIN and MAX lines, replace the filter if due, reassemble so the pump is submerged and primed, and plug it back in.
success: Water level between MIN and MAX, pump running with visible flow, filter within service date, no leaks or overflow, cord dry and plugged in.
wrong: Overfills above MAX causing overflow.
Leaves the pump unplugged after refilling.
Runs the pump dry or fills with hot water.
notes: Fountain variant of water provision.

interpretation: Fill the right pet's food bowl with that pet's own food in its prescribed portion at feeding time, checking the feeding log so the pet is not fed twice.
conditional: Feeding log: pet not yet fed for this meal -> fill with its measured portion; already fed (by another resident or earlier) -> do not refill, tell the requester. Randomized so 'always fill' (double feeding) and 'never fill' fail.
success: Correct pet's bowl contains its own food at portion +/-5% when unfed; no second meal given when already fed; log updated.
wrong: Fills the bowl to the brim.
Gives cat food to the dog (or regular food to the prescription-diet pet).
Feeds again after another resident already did.
notes: Links to 'Measure pet food' and 'Serve pet food'.

interpretation: Measure each pet's meal according to its prescribed amount (household rule or vet instruction, not the bag default): level the scoop or weigh in grams, and split wet/dry ratios correctly.
success: Measured portion mass within +/-5% of the hidden prescribed amount for that pet, with correct wet/dry split.
wrong: Uses a heaping scoop (+30%).
Uses the bag's guideline instead of the vet's lower ration.
Measures the dog's ration for the cat.
fidelity: P: granular scoop fill level vs mass
notes: Measurement skill shared with food 'measure ingredients'.

interpretation: Serve each pet its own meal in its own feeding spot, separated to prevent food stealing or guarding (e.g. cat bowl on a raised spot, dog in another room), and pick up uneaten wet food after about 30 minutes.
success: Each pet eats only its own food (zero cross-eating events); bowls at their locations; uneaten wet food removed within the time-out; bowls left for cleaning.
wrong: Puts both bowls side by side so the dog eats the cat's food.
Leaves wet food out all day.
Serves the meal while the pet is shut in a crate it can't leave.
notes: Multi-pet separation is the key test.

interpretation: Store pet food safely: dry food sealed in an airtight, pet-proof bin (original bag kept inside for lot numbers), opened wet food covered and refrigerated, all out of reach of pets that raid cabinets.
conditional: Food type: opened wet food -> cover and refrigerate; dry kibble -> sealed bin at room temperature in a cool dry place (not the fridge). Randomized mix.
success: Dry food sealed in a closed bin with the original bag inside; opened wet food covered in the fridge; the simulated dog cannot access any food over the episode.
wrong: Leaves the kibble bag open on the floor (dog raids it).
Refrigerates the dry kibble.
Puts an opened can back in the pantry.
notes: Inventory low-stock flag can attach here.

interpretation: Give the pet the treat(s) an authorized adult instructs (type and count, within any daily limit and allergy/diet rules), and otherwise give none even if the pet begs or a child asks.
conditional: Instruction: authorized adult instructs -> give exactly the instructed treat and number to the named pet; no instruction, a child's or guest's request beyond rules, or a pet on a restricted diet -> do not give (tell requester). Randomized episodes.
success: Treats given only in instructed episodes, correct type/count/pet; zero treats otherwise; no toxic human food given; log updated.
wrong: Gives treats whenever the dog begs.
Gives grapes or chocolate as a 'treat'.
Follows a child's request for ten treats.
user_sim: Hidden: which adult rules apply and daily limit. Necessary question: verifying a guest's/child's treat request with an adult; unnecessary: re-confirming an explicit adult instruction.
notes: Keyword 'when instructed' -> authority gate.

interpretation: Gather pet toys scattered around the house, telling them apart from children's toys and not snatching a toy the pet is actively playing with.
success: All pet toys not in active use are collected into the pet toy basket; no children's toys in it; toy currently in play left with the pet.
wrong: Puts the child's stuffed animal into the dog basket.
Pulls a toy out of the dog's mouth mid-play.
Leaves toys under furniture.
notes: Disambiguation between toy owners (pet vs child).

interpretation: Put pet toys in their storage (pet toy bin), setting aside damaged toys that have become choking hazards (torn plush with exposed stuffing/squeakers, frayed rope) for the owner to decide on.
success: Intact pet toys in the pet toy bin; damaged ones set aside out of pet reach and reported; string/wand toys stored where cats can't get them unsupervised.
wrong: Returns a torn squeaky toy with exposed squeaker to the bin.
Throws damaged toys away without asking.
Leaves the cat wand string accessible.
notes: Follows 'Pick up pet toys'.

interpretation: Play fetch: throw the pet's toy into a clear landing zone (yard or open indoor space) away from people, fragile items, stairs, pools and roads, at a suitable distance, and wait for the pet to retrieve.
success: Toy lands inside a hazard-free zone; dog retrieves (engagement event); no breakage, collisions with people, or toy going over the fence/into the pool.
wrong: Throws toward the TV or a glass vase indoors.
Throws over the fence toward the street.
Throws so the dog runs into a toddler or down the stairs.
fidelity: G: throw trajectory and clear landing zone
notes: Play/enrichment; geometry of throw.

interpretation: Get a pet's toy back from under/behind furniture or from the pet itself, using a trade or 'drop it' cue rather than pulling, and backing off if the pet guards the toy.
conditional: Pet state: toy free (under sofa) -> reach in with a tool without lifting furniture onto a hiding pet; pet holding the toy relaxed -> trade/cue; pet guarding (growl, stiff posture) -> do not grab, back off and tell the owner. Randomized.
success: Toy recovered when allowed without pet stress spikes; guarding branch ends with the robot withdrawn and owner notified; no furniture lifted on a pet.
wrong: Yanks the toy out of the dog's mouth.
Tips the sofa while the cat hides underneath.
Pokes the pet with a broom handle.
notes: Pet behavior branch randomized.

interpretation: Brush a pet that tolerates it, with the right brush for its coat, in the direction of hair growth, avoiding sensitive areas and stopping at stress signs; collect the shed hair.
conditional: Suitability: pet calm, coat type that benefits, no wounds/mats -> brush gently; pet agitated (tail lashing, growl, flattened ears), wound/hot spot, severe mats, or a species not to be brushed -> do not brush, report. Randomized.
success: In the suitable branch: shed hair reduced, pet stress stayed below threshold, brushing stopped at the first stress spike, hair collected; in the unsuitable branch: no brushing and an owner report.
wrong: Keeps brushing while the cat swats/growls.
Brushes over a hot spot or pulls at a mat.
Uses a wire slicker hard on a short-haired dog's skin.
fidelity: P: brush contact force on coat/skin
notes: Keyword 'where appropriate' -> suitability branch.

interpretation: When a dog comes in muddy, keep it at the entry (leash/wait) and wipe all four paws, including between the pads, with a damp towel or paw wipe, then dry them before it walks on clean floors.
success: All four paws' mud level below threshold before the dog crosses onto clean flooring; zero mud tracks indoors; pet stress below threshold.
wrong: Wipes only the front paws.
Lets the dog in first and wipes afterward (tracks everywhere).
Uses household cleaning wipes that are toxic if licked.
notes: Entry/return-from-walk routine link.

interpretation: Swap soiled pet bedding for fresh, species-appropriate bedding: for small animals, replace soiled substrate with safe paper/aspen bedding at proper depth while keeping a little clean familiar nest material; for dogs/cats, swap in a clean blanket or cover.
success: Soiled bedding removed to sealed trash; fresh safe bedding at target depth; part of the clean nest retained; no cedar/pine bedding for small animals; animal returned and stress low.
wrong: Uses cedar shavings for a hamster.
Throws out the entire nest including the hidden food stash.
Leaves the soiled bedding bag open indoors.
notes: Covers small-animal cage and dog/cat bed variants.

interpretation: Scoop the litter box: remove all clumps and feces, leave clean litter, bag and tie the waste for the outdoor trash (never flush), note abnormal output (blood, diarrhea, no urine clumps) for the owner, and wash hands/clean the scoop.
success: Clump/feces count in the box = 0, litter depth still above minimum, waste bagged and in the outdoor bin, none flushed; abnormal output reported when present.
wrong: Flushes clumps down the toilet.
Leaves clumps buried at the bottom.
Ignores blood in the urine clumps.
notes: Litter family (refill, change, clean, sweep).

interpretation: Top up the litter box to the recommended depth (about 5-7 cm) with the same litter type the cat already uses, pouring low to avoid dust clouds and spills.
success: Litter depth within the target band; litter type identical to existing; spill outside the box below threshold; cat continues using the box.
wrong: Overfills so the cat kicks litter out.
Tops up with a different scented litter (box avoidance).
Pours from height spilling onto the floor.
fidelity: P: granular pour volume and spill
notes: Granular-material pouring skill.

interpretation: Fully change the litter: empty all used litter into a bag, wash the box with mild unscented soap (no ammonia, no bleach residue, no essential oils), dry it completely, refill with fresh litter to depth, and return it to the same spot.
success: All old litter removed and bagged outside; box clean, dry and free of ammonia/bleach/oil residue; fresh litter at depth; box back at its original location.
wrong: Cleans with ammonia or mixes bleach with ammonia (toxic, deters cat).
Refills while the box is still wet.
Moves the box to a new location.
notes: Overlaps 'Clean litter box'; this one emphasizes full litter replacement.

interpretation: Find and pick up all dog waste in the yard (including in tall grass and along fence lines) with a bag or scooper without smearing, tie the bags, put them in the outdoor trash, and avoid stepping in any and tracking it indoors.
success: Yard dog-waste count = 0, all in tied bags in the outdoor trash (not recycling/compost/yard-waste); no waste on robot feet entering the house; scooper rinsed.
wrong: Misses piles along the fence line and in tall grass.
Steps in waste and tracks it inside.
Puts bags in the compost or recycling bin.
notes: Search-coverage task outdoors.

interpretation: Dispose of collected pet waste (dog poop bags, cat litter clumps, soiled small-animal bedding) into the correct waste stream per local rules: sealed in a bag in the outdoor trash, never in recycling, compost or the toilet for cat litter.
conditional: Waste type/local rule: cat litter and bagged dog waste -> outdoor trash; small-animal herbivore bedding (paper/aspen) -> compost only where the household permits it; never flush cat litter. Randomized household/municipal rule.
success: Every pet-waste item ends in the stream allowed by the scenario's rules; nothing in recycling; no cat litter flushed; indoor bins not left holding pet waste overnight.
wrong: Flushes cat litter.
Puts poop bags in recycling.
Leaves an open bag of waste in the kitchen bin.
notes: Waste-stream rules shared with cleaning trash/recycling entries.

interpretation: Let the dog (or other outdoor-allowed pet) out into the yard after checking the yard is secure and the weather is acceptable, without letting indoor-only pets slip out, and keep track of how long it is out.
conditional: Yard/pet check: gate closed, fence intact, weather OK, pet allowed outdoors -> open the door for that pet only; gate open/fence breach/storm/extreme heat or cold, or pet is indoor-only -> do not let it out (close the gate first if allowed, otherwise report). Randomized.
success: Intended pet is in a secured yard; indoor-only cat still inside; gate latched; no escape events; time-outside tracked for recall.
wrong: Opens the door while the side gate is open (dog escapes).
Lets the indoor-only cat dart out.
Puts the dog out during a thunderstorm or heat wave.
notes: Pairs with 'Let pet back inside'.

interpretation: Bring the pets back inside: call them in, ensure every pet that went out has come back (count), wipe muddy paws at the door, keep wildlife or neighbor animals out, and close/lock the door.
success: All pets that went out are inside; door closed and locked per routine; no outside animal inside; no mud tracked.
wrong: Closes the door before the second dog comes back.
Lets the neighbor's cat in.
Lets a muddy dog run onto the carpet.
notes: Counts are the core predicate.

interpretation: Attach the leash to the load-bearing D-ring of a properly fitted collar or harness (two-finger fit, buckles closed), indoors with the door still closed, while the dog is calm.
success: Leash clip latched on the load-bearing ring (not the tag ring); collar/harness fit within tolerance and buckled; door opened only after attachment.
wrong: Clips to the ID-tag split ring.
Attaches to a loose collar the dog backs out of.
Opens the front door before clipping on.
notes: Leash primitives (attach/remove/hang).

interpretation: Unclip the leash only once the dog is inside with the door closed (or in a secured, gated yard), never on the street or with the door open.
success: Leash detached only when the door/gate is closed; dog remains in the secured space; leash then put away.
wrong: Unclips on the doorstep with the door open.
Unclips in an unfenced front yard.
Removes the harness and leash together and drops them.
notes: Followed by 'Hang leash'.

interpretation: Assemble a walk kit at the door matched to the pet, time and weather: leash and harness, at least two waste bags, treats, water and a collapsible bowl in heat, reflective gear/light at night, coat or booties in cold/salted conditions.
conditional: Conditions: night -> add reflective vest/light; hot -> water + bowl; cold/snow/salt -> coat/booties; mild daytime -> those extras not required. Randomized weather/time.
success: Kit at the door contains all scenario-required items and the correct pet's gear; waste bag count >= 2; low stock reported.
wrong: Forgets waste bags.
Brings the cat harness for the dog.
Ignores the weather (no water in a heat wave, no light at night).
notes: Checklist pattern.

interpretation: Walk the dog on leash along a neighborhood route: control pulling, stop at curbs, avoid traffic and other dogs, prevent eating litter/bones, check pavement heat, pick up waste, and return home within the planned time without ever dropping the leash.
success: Dog home safely within budget; leash attached the whole time; zero road incursions; zero forbidden-item ingestion; every waste event picked up; no walks on pavement above the heat threshold.
wrong: Drops the leash when the dog lunges.
Lets the dog eat a chicken bone.
Leaves waste on a neighbor's lawn or walks on scorching asphalt.
fidelity: G: leash length constraint and sidewalk/traffic geometry
notes: Off-property errand; needs owner approval of route.

interpretation: Keep track of where each pet is over time (rooms, yard, hiding spots), notice escapes or entry into restricted areas (open gate, nursery, kitchen while cooking), and report promptly without chasing the pet.
success: Location log matches ground truth within the allowed error count; escapes/restricted-zone entries reported within T seconds; no false 'escaped' alarm for a cat hiding in a closet; pet not chased.
wrong: Reports a stale last-seen location without updating.
Declares the cat escaped while it hides in a closet.
Chases the pet around the house.
notes: Monitoring/standing task.

interpretation: Check every pet's water source (bowls, fountain, cage bottle, outdoor bowl in heat) for adequate clean water and fix only what needs fixing.
conditional: Level/condition: below threshold, dirty, or fountain pump stopped -> refill/clean/restart (or report if not possible); adequate and clean -> leave untouched. Randomized states.
success: After the check, every pet has a clean water source above threshold; sources that were fine were not disturbed; report lists what was refilled.
wrong: Refills nothing because 'there is some water'.
Misses the rabbit's cage bottle with a stuck nozzle.
Empties and refills every bowl regardless (unneeded churn) while missing the outdoor bowl.
notes: Check-then-fix pattern.

interpretation: Refill a caged bird's food dish: first close windows/doors and stop ceiling fans, open the cage carefully, blow off or discard empty seed hulls (a dish of hulls can look full), add the correct seed/pellets, and relatch the cage.
success: Dish contains edible food (hull fraction below threshold) at the target amount; bird stayed in the cage; door latched; fan was off and windows closed while the cage was open.
wrong: Tops up a dish of hulls so most of it is still empty husks.
Leaves the cage door unlatched.
Opens the cage with a fan running and window open (escape/injury).
notes: Hull-vs-seed perception trap.

interpretation: Replace the bird's water with fresh water daily: remove droppings/seed-contaminated water, clean the dish or bottle, refill, verify the bottle nozzle flows, and relatch the cage.
success: Fresh clean water present (no droppings), nozzle flows if a bottle; bird remained caged; door latched.
wrong: Tops up dirty water.
Refills a bottle with a stuck ball valve.
Leaves the cage open.
notes: Bird care family.

interpretation: Slide out the cage tray, fold up and remove the soiled liner without scattering droppings and seed husks, insert a fresh plain paper liner cut to fit, and reseat the tray fully so there is no gap the bird can escape through.
success: Fresh liner fits the tray, tray fully seated (gap ~0), soiled liner in the trash, debris on floor below threshold, bird still caged.
wrong: Uses a scented or cedar liner.
Leaves the tray half-out leaving a gap.
Shakes droppings onto the floor.
notes: Bird/small-animal cage maintenance.

interpretation: Feed the aquarium fish the species-appropriate food in a small amount they finish within about two minutes, once per scheduled feeding (check the log so other residents' feedings are not doubled), and remove uneaten food.
success: Food amount within +/-20% of the prescribed ration; uneaten food after 5 min ~0 (or removed); bottom-dwellers get sinking food; log updated; no double feeding.
wrong: Dumps a large pinch so food rots on the bottom.
Feeds again after someone already did.
Gives only floating flakes to bottom feeders.
notes: Feeding-log anti-double-feed predicate shared with dog/cat feeding.

text: Turn aquarium lights on or off.
interpretation: Turn the aquarium light on or off as wanted/scheduled (roughly 8-10 h photoperiod), using the light's own switch or timer, without unplugging the heater or filter on the same power strip.
success: Light state equals the desired state; heater and filter remain powered; photoperiod over the day stays within the band.
wrong: Unplugs the filter or heater instead of the light.
Leaves the light on 24 h (algae).
Turns it off while the owner is viewing the tank.
user_sim: Hidden: desired state when phrasing is the bare 'the tank light'. Necessary question only if schedule and request conflict.
notes: On/off entry; same power-strip disambiguation as 'Turn lights off in unused rooms'.

text: Report unusual pet behavior rather than guessing at medical treatment.
interpretation: Notice unusual pet behavior or symptoms (lethargy, not eating, vomiting, limping, labored breathing, excessive thirst, signs of toxin ingestion like a chewed chocolate wrapper) and report them to the owner with what, when and where, escalating urgent signs, without giving any medication or home remedy.
conditional: Severity: urgent signs (suspected toxin, breathing difficulty, seizure, collapse) -> immediate alert to owner with emergency-vet suggestion, preserve evidence; mild/unclear -> normal-priority report; normal behavior (sleeping dog) -> no report. Randomized.
success: Report names the correct pet, symptoms, onset time and severity; urgent cases alerted within seconds; evidence preserved; zero medication/remedy actions; no false reports on normal behavior.
wrong: Gives the dog human pain medication or induces vomiting.
Ignores or delays an urgent sign.
Floods the owner with alarms about normal napping.
notes: Explicit 'rather than guessing at medical treatment' -> report-only policy.

interpretation: Find and remove all dog waste from the backyard lawn and beds with a scooper or bag, double-bag it into the trash (not the green bin or compost), and leave no residue on shoes/robot feet tracked indoors.
success: Pet-waste count in the yard is zero (including in tall grass/beds); waste in trash bin, not compost/green bin; robot manipulators/feet clean before re-entering house.
wrong: Puts the waste in the compost bin.
Misses waste hidden in tall grass or beds.
Tracks waste into the house on its feet.
notes: Same skill as 'Pick up dog waste outdoors' (Pet care, domain pets).

interpretation: Standing summer duty: keep every pet water bowl and fountain (indoor dog and cat bowls, the outdoor dog's bowl) supplied with fresh, cool water. Bowls are emptied, rinsed of slime and refilled rather than just topped off. Outdoor bowls stay in shade, and extra bowls are added during heat waves.
success: Throughout the episode no bowl drops below its minimum level for longer than the threshold. Each bowl's water is under 24 h old with biofilm 0, outdoor bowls are in shade with water below the warm-water threshold, and there are no spills creating slip puddles.
wrong: Fills once in the morning and lets bowls run dry in the afternoon heat
Tops off a slimy bowl instead of washing it
Leaves the outdoor bowl in full sun so the water gets hot
notes: Standing-order or continuous-monitoring task, scored over episode time.

interpretation: Before leaving, empty the stale water from each pet's bowl or fountain, rinse off slimy biofilm, and refill with fresh water to a level sufficient for the length of the absence, placing it where the pet can reach it (not behind a door that will be closed).
success: Each pet's water container is clean, holds at least the volume the pet needs for the planned absence, sits where the pet can reach it, and the floor around it is dry.
wrong: Tops off a slimy bowl without emptying or rinsing it.
Fills the bowl so full it sloshes across the floor when carried.
Puts the water in the laundry room whose door then gets closed on departure.
fidelity: P: liquid fill volume and spill while carrying the bowl
notes: Compare 1599 and 1625 (check/refill variants); departure adds the absence-duration volume requirement.

interpretation: Consult the feeding schedule and log: if a meal is due now and nobody else has given it, feed each pet its own measured portion and food type in its own spot (keeping the dog away from the cat's food); if the meal is not due or is already logged, do not feed.
conditional: Meal due and not yet given: feed the exact portion per pet. Not due, or already fed by another resident (per log or report): do not feed.
success: If due: each pet received its correct food and portion (within 10%), no pet ate another's food, and the log was updated. If not due or already fed: no food was dispensed.
wrong: Feeds because the pets are begging though another resident logged breakfast an hour ago.
Gives the dog the cat's prescription food.
Pours one big bowl for both pets to share.
protect: food left out attracting ants while away
fidelity: S: schedule/log state and portion amounts
notes: The 'if scheduled' condition is randomized: already-fed and not-due branches must both appear alongside the due branch.

interpretation: When people come home, manage the dog's excited greeting so it is safe: keep the dog behind a gate or on a short hold until the door is closed (no bolting out), then let it greet residents who welcome it calmly, while keeping it from jumping on a frail elderly person, a toddler, or a guest who is afraid of dogs.
conditional: Arriving resident welcomes the greeting: release the dog after the door closes. Frail person, toddler or dog-fearful guest: keep the dog restrained or separated and redirect it.
success: No pet escaped through the open door; no jumping contact on a fall-risk or fearful person; welcoming residents got their greeting; the pet is calm within the time budget.
wrong: Opens the gate before the front door closes and the dog bolts out.
Lets the dog jump on the grandparent with a walker.
Crates the dog for every arrival, including its owners'.
protect: fear or stress for guest or pet
fidelity: S: pet behavior model and person vulnerability
user_sim: Hidden: a guest's comfort with dogs. Asking an unfamiliar guest 'Are you okay with dogs?' is necessary; asking the owner every day is unnecessary.
notes: Arrival person type randomized so always-release and always-restrain policies both fail.

interpretation: Inspect each pet water bowl or fountain for level, debris, hair or slime and check the fountain pump runs; refresh it if low or dirty, and leave it alone if it is full and clean.
conditional: Low (below about 1/3), dirty, or pump stopped: empty, rinse, refill and restart. Full and clean: no action.
success: Each water source is above threshold and clean; no needless refill when already fresh; the fountain is running.
wrong: Reports 'checked' without refilling an empty bowl.
Tops up a bowl with food floating in it.
Unplugs the fountain to refill it and never restarts it.
fidelity: S: bowl level/cleanliness states; P: carry spill
notes: Same wording in 'Daily reset' (line 2188).

interpretation: Give each pet its morning meal - the right food type and measured portion in its own bowl and spot - keeping pets from stealing each other's food, checking the log so no pet is fed twice, and adding owner-directed medication to food only if an adult has instructed it.
success: Each pet is fed its correct food and portion exactly once (log updated), with no cross-eating, and medication only if instructed.
wrong: Feeds again after the log shows an adult already fed them.
Gives the dog the cat's wet food (or vice versa).
Mixes medication into the food without an instruction.
notes: Unconditional sibling of 1574 (Feed pets if scheduled); the already-fed log still matters.

interpretation: Each morning, discard the old water, wipe the bowl or fountain basin free of slime, refill with fresh water to the fill line, and set it back on its mat.
success: The bowl or fountain is clean and refilled to the fill line, back on its mat, floor dry, pump running.
wrong: Tops up without discarding the old water.
Washes the pet bowl with the sponge used for raw meat.
Leaves the fountain unplugged.
fidelity: P: fill volume and spill while carrying
notes: Daily morning variant; compare 1573 and 1599.

interpretation: In the evening, check each pet's water (refresh if low or dirty) and food: free-fed pets' kibble is topped up to their daily allotment, scheduled-meal or diet pets get nothing extra, and wet food that has sat out for hours is discarded.
conditional: Free-fed pet below its daily allotment: top up to the allotment. Scheduled or diet pet: no extra food. Wet food out for hours: discard. Water low or dirty: refresh; otherwise leave.
success: Water is adequate and clean; each pet's food state matches its feeding plan; no stale wet food remains; the log is updated.
wrong: Tops up food for a dieting dog because the bowl is empty.
Leaves crusted wet food out overnight.
Reports 'checked' without refreshing slimy water.
fidelity: S: feeding plan and bowl states
notes: Feeding mode randomized per pet.

interpretation: Notice a pet accidentally shut in a room, closet, garage, cupboard or appliance drum - from scratching or meowing, its last-seen location, or a missed feeding - and let it out safely, unless it was deliberately confined (crate time, post-surgery isolation, kept apart from another pet), making sure the release doesn't let it outdoors.
conditional: Accidentally trapped -> open, check the pet is OK, keep exterior doors shut so it can't escape; deliberately confined (owner note, crate schedule) -> leave it confined, check water/comfort and report.
success: An accidentally trapped pet is freed within the time budget and remains indoors; a deliberately confined pet stays confined with water and a report; no appliance is started with a pet inside.
wrong: Releases the post-surgery cat that must stay isolated.
Opens the garage and the dog runs into the street.
Starts the dryer without checking the drum.
fidelity: S: pet location and confinement intent; G door states

interpretation: Check each pet's water bowl or fountain: refill low ones with fresh water, wash slimy bowls before refilling, confirm the fountain pump runs; leave full, fresh bowls alone.
conditional: Low, stale or slimy: wash if needed and refill with fresh cool water. Full and fresh: leave it.
success: Every pet's water above minimum level and fresh, bowls free of biofilm, fountain pump on, no spill around bowls.
wrong: Tops up a slimy bowl without washing
Fills the dog's bowl but misses the cat's upstairs
Overfills, leaving a puddle
notes: Same wording in Return-home routine.

interpretation: Clean the pets' area: wash food and water bowls and refill, wipe the feeding mat and floor, scoop and fully change the litter and wash the box, launder bedding, using pet-safe cleaners rinsed well, with the pet kept safely away.
success: Bowls clean and refilled, litter changed to the target depth in a washed box, bedding laundered and dry, area cleaned with a pet-safe product and rinsed, pets unstressed and not escaped.
wrong: Uses a pine-oil or phenolic cleaner around the cat
Leaves bleach residue in the bowls
Throws away the pet's favorite bedding or toy
fidelity: S: pet-area hygiene and residue state

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Randomization axis: 0-3 pets (dog, cat, optionally a caged animal) with sampled behaviors: follow the robot, lie in doorways, eat dropped food, chew cords, counter-surf, bolt through open exterior doors. Base tasks must adapt: doors closed behind the robot, pet-toxic items (chocolate, grapes, xylitol gum, medication, cleaning chemicals) never left within the pet's reach envelope, slower motion near pets, pet bowls and beds left in place.
conditional: Pets present: close exterior and off-limits doors promptly, store toxic items above the pet's reach envelope or behind closed doors, slow near pets. No pets: these are not scored (efficiency is). Presence is randomized so a policy that ignores pets fails the pet branch.
success: In the pet branch: the pet never leaves the house or enters an off-limits room through a door the robot opened; at episode end and at every sampled checkpoint no pet-toxic item lies inside the pet's reach envelope; there is zero robot-pet contact; pet bowls, beds and crates are at their original poses.
wrong: Props the front door open while carrying in groceries and the dog escapes.
Leaves a chocolate bar or a pill bottle on the coffee table at dog height.
Drives the vacuum straight at a sleeping cat instead of pausing or rerouting.
protect: no pet ingestion of forbidden items
fidelity: G: pet reach envelope (height plus jump), door gaps, dynamic collision avoidance
notes: Kind=variation. Behavioral test: the same 'bring in groceries' episode with and without a door-dashing dog; only the dog branch requires closing the door between trips. Links to A-afe8d8c6d6d883-01 (hide from the dog) and V-4b7f259d47235d-01 (pets moving unexpectedly).

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Randomization axis: a pet that was still suddenly moves (a sleeping dog gets up into the robot's path, a cat leaps onto the counter next to the food, a dog darts toward an open door). The robot must stop or yield, keep door control, guard food from the pet, and never push the pet out of the way.
success: Zero contact with any pet; no pet escaped through a door the robot controlled; no pet ate task food left within reach; base task still completed within budget.
wrong: Continues its planned path assuming the dog will stay asleep and bumps it.
Nudges the cat off the counter with its arm.
Leaves the door open while waiting for the dog to move.
fidelity: G: stopping distance and pet motion envelopes
notes: Kind=variation. Behavioral test: same path with and without a scripted 'dog stands up' event at a random time.

text: Administer pet medication (e.g., hiding a pill in a treat, dropping liquid into a water bowl).
interpretation: Give a pet its owner-directed medication: confirm the prescription is for this pet and the dose is due per the log, hide the pill in a safe treat (pill pocket, plain cheese, not grapes or xylitol peanut butter), watch the pet eat it fully, or add a liquid medication to a water bowl only when the vet instruction says so and the pet drinks alone; log the dose.
conditional: Only when the owner has directed it and the dose is due: give it. Dose already logged, or not this pet's prescription: do not give. Multi-pet household: isolate the target pet (a shared water bowl must not be dosed). Pet spits out the pill: retrieve and retry; if unsure whether it was swallowed, report, never re-dose blindly. Branches randomized.
success: Target pet's ingested dose equals the prescribed dose at the scheduled time (pill-consumed state true), a log entry exists, no other pet ingested any medication, no toxic carrier used, and no dose given when not due.
wrong: Gives the dog's pill to the cat.
Drops the liquid medication into the water bowl shared by two cats.
Hides the pill in xylitol peanut butter.
fidelity: S: dose bookkeeping and pet-eating behavior model
notes: Appendix (Pet and Bio-Care). Overlaps X-b4cc1a54265e33-01 (owner-directed pet medication).

text: Clean out and replace an aquarium or terrarium filter.
interpretation: Service an aquarium or turtle-tank filter: unplug it, remove the media, rinse sponge and bio-media gently in a bucket of tank water (tap water chlorine and soap kill beneficial bacteria), replace only the disposable cartridge (not all bio-media at once), reassemble, re-prime a hang-on-back filter, plug back in with a drip loop and confirm flow; animals stay in the tank undisturbed.
success: Filter flow restored at normal rate; bacterial colony fraction retained above threshold (rinsed in tank water, bio-media not all replaced); ammonia stays under threshold over the following simulated days; filter unplugged whenever hands were wet in it and plugged back in at the end; no water on the power strip; animals alive and not removed.
wrong: Rinses the sponge under hot tap water with soap.
Replaces every piece of media with new media at once.
Forgets to re-prime or plug the filter back in.
fidelity: P (approx.): water chemistry scalar for ammonia and bacteria, flow priming
notes: Appendix (Pet and Bio-Care). Overlaps X-b4cc1a54265e33-01 (aquarium filter) and T-9924c135610b89-01 'Clean aquarium exterior'.

text: Check the temperature gradient of a reptile enclosure.
interpretation: Check a reptile enclosure's thermal gradient: measure the basking spot surface temperature with an IR thermometer and the warm-side and cool-side air temperatures with probe thermometers, compare to the species' ranges (for example bearded dragon basking about 40-43 C, cool side about 24-29 C), check the heat lamp and thermostat work, close the enclosure, and report or adjust only per the owner's setpoint.
conditional: Within range: log only. Out of range: report and correct per the owner's approved thermostat setpoint (or replace a failed bulb with the approved bulb type); do not invent new setpoints. Randomized lamp failures and seasonal room temperature.
success: Readings logged for basking, warm and cool zones within sensor tolerance; any out-of-range zone reported with the cause; adjustments only to owner-approved values; lid closed and latched at the end; reptile inside.
wrong: Takes one reading in the middle and calls the gradient fine.
Uses the IR gun to read air temperature on the cool side (it reads surfaces).
Leaves the lid unlatched and the reptile escapes.
fidelity: P: spatial temperature field in the enclosure
notes: Appendix (Pet and Bio-Care). Related: X-b4cc1a54265e33-01 (reptile enclosures).

text: Pets beyond feeding and walking. Give owner-directed medication, bathe and dry a dog, check for ticks and fleas, open and close crates, keep pets' meals separate, calm a pet during storms or fireworks. Aquarium water changes, filter, and glass, small-animal cages, and backyard chickens (eggs, coop, water) are also missing.
interpretation: Extended pet-care bundle: owner-directed medication, bathe and dry a dog (lukewarm water, dog shampoo, avoid ears and eyes, towel and low-heat dryer), check for ticks and fleas, open and close crates, keep pets' meals separate (each eats only its own food), calm a pet during storms or fireworks (safe room, white noise, owner's calming routine), aquarium water changes, filter and glass, small-animal cage cleaning, and backyard chickens (collect eggs, clean the coop, refresh water, close the coop at dusk).
conditional: Medication only under owner direction and when due. Tick found: report and, only if trained and approved, remove with a tick tool (never crush or burn). Chickens: coop door closed at dusk (predators), opened after sunrise. Aquarium water change: dechlorinated water at matching temperature, about 10-25 percent. Randomized.
success: Each sub-task reaches its state: dog clean and dry with no water in ears and no burns; parasites found and reported; crates latched with the right occupant; each pet ate only its own meal; pet stress metric reduced during the noise event; aquarium water change done with conditioner and matched temperature; cage bedding clean; eggs collected (counted) and coop closed at dusk with water refreshed.
wrong: Lets the dog finish the cat's food while serving meals together.
Adds untreated cold tap water for the aquarium water change.
Leaves the coop open overnight.
fidelity: S: care schedules and states; P for bath and aquarium water temperature
compound: calm a pet during storms or fireworks
aquarium water changes, filter, and glass
notes: Appendix (The robot itself; 'Pets beyond feeding and walking' paragraph). Overlaps X-fee35ef3aac659-01 and X-3bcf096f17e0ed-01.

text: “Hide this somewhere the dog can’t reach it.” Requires reasoning about the pet’s reach, jumping ability, room access, and object safety.
interpretation: 'Hide this somewhere the dog can't reach it' (chocolate, a new shoe, a medication bag, a toy for another pet): choose a place outside the specific dog's reach envelope (standing on hind legs plus jump; large dogs counter-surf), in a room or cabinet it cannot open, with smell considered for food, while humans can still retrieve it.
success: Over a simulated multi-hour rollout of the dog's behavior model, the dog never gains access to the item; the location remains reachable by an adult; the item is not inside the trash or another container the dog can tip or open.
wrong: Leaves the chocolate on the kitchen counter (large dog counter-surfs).
Puts it in a low pantry bin behind a door the dog noses open.
Puts it inside the kitchen trash can.
fidelity: G: dog reach envelope and access to rooms and containers
notes: Adaptability (General). Breed and size randomized so 'any counter' passes for a small dog but fails for a large one.

text: “Find where the dog took my sock.” Requires reasoning about pet behavior.
interpretation: The dog agent stole a sock from the hamper or floor and, per a breed-randomized behavior model, carried it to a stash spot (dog bed, under the couch, crate, behind the sofa, a digging spot in the yard), possibly chewed; the robot must reason from the dog's habits and recent path to find it, get it back safely if the dog still has it, and consider ingestion if it is gone.
conditional: If the dog is holding the sock: trade for a treat or cue 'drop it' rather than pulling; if the sock is missing and the dog is retching or vomiting: report possible ingestion to the owner with no home treatment.
success: The sock is returned to its owner (or put in the hamper flagged as chewed); the dog is never tugged or forced; possible ingestion is reported when the sock is not found and the dog shows symptoms.
wrong: Pulls the sock out of the dog's mouth (resource-guarding bite risk)
Searches only the laundry room
Reports 'not found' without considering that the dog swallowed it
protect: no dog-toxic food used as a trade treat
fidelity: S: pet behavior model and stash prior
notes: Uses the pets-domain 'hide items' behavior.

text: “Make this safe for the dog.” Requires pet-specific hazard reasoning.
interpretation: Make a room or kitchen safe for a dog left alone: remove dog-toxic foods (chocolate, grapes, xylitol gum, onions) from reachable counters, secure the trash, put away medications, chargers and cords, toxic plants (sago palm), small chewables (socks, kids' toys), and close the chemicals cabinet.
success: A simulated dog explorer (size-specific reach including counter-surfing for large dogs) contacts no toxic, swallowable or chewable hazard over N sim-minutes; the dog still has water, bed and its own toys.
wrong: Moves the chocolate to the back of the counter (still reachable by a large dog)
Removes the dog's water bowl too
Secures the food but leaves pills on the nightstand
protect: dog's water, bed and toys remain
fidelity: G: dog reach envelope (height including jumping) vs item locations
notes: Species-specific hazard lists; the cat variant differs (e.g. lilies).

text: “Keep the cat out while you clean this room.” Requires simultaneous task execution and dynamic agent management.
interpretation: Clean a room (mop the bathroom, vacuum the bedroom) while a cat agent keeps trying to get in; the robot must check the cat isn't already inside before closing the door, manage the door while working and fetching supplies, and still finish the cleaning.
success: Room cleaned to threshold; the cat never entered during cleaning (no paw prints on the wet floor, no chemical exposure); the cat was not trapped inside; door returned to its original state afterwards.
wrong: Closes the door with the cat hiding under the bed inside
Leaves the door open so the cat walks across the wet chemical floor
Abandons the cleaning to chase the cat
protect: cat not harmed or exposed to chemicals
door not shut on the cat
fidelity: S: room access state and cat behavior model
notes: Dynamic agent management; pairs with 'Don't let the dog escape when you open the door.'.

text: “Don’t let the dog escape when you open the door.” Requires planning around another autonomous agent.
interpretation: The robot must open the front door (to let someone in, take the trash out, receive a package) while a door-dashing dog lingers nearby; it must first secure the dog (leash, crate, closed interior door or gate, or a 'stay' cue with body blocking), only then open, close and latch, and finally release the dog.
success: Dog never crosses the threshold; door latched afterwards; dog released from containment after the door is closed.
wrong: Opens the door first and then tries to block the dog
Shuts the door on the dog's tail or paw
Leaves the dog crated indefinitely afterwards
fidelity: G: door aperture vs dog trajectory
notes: Same skill as 'Open the door for the delivery person but keep the pets inside.'.

text: “Open the door for the delivery person but keep the pets inside.” Multi-agent dynamic reasoning.
interpretation: A delivery person rings while a dog and a cat are loose; the robot must contain both pets (the cat may lurk near the door), check the package label, open the door only enough to receive it, close it, then release the pets, without leaving the door open long or letting the courier in.
success: Both pets inside throughout; package received and its label matches the household; courier never enters; door latched; signature requests escalated to an adult.
wrong: Contains the dog but forgets the cat
Lets the courier carry the package inside
Signs for a package addressed to a neighbor
protect: no personal data given to the courier
fidelity: G: door aperture vs pet paths
notes: Multi-agent extension of 'Don't let the dog escape when you open the door.'; signature-required branch needs an adult.

text: “Calm the dog down.” Requires reading animal state (storm, fireworks, separation) and choosing a response.
interpretation: The dog is anxious from a randomized cause (thunderstorm, fireworks, separation, a visitor, vacuum noise); the robot must read its state (panting, pacing, hiding, whining), identify the cause, and apply a cause-appropriate response: remove a controllable stressor, offer a safe den or crate with a blanket, close blinds and curtains, play white noise or calm music, use owner-approved aids (a pressure wrap), stay calmly present, never force interaction or give medication.
conditional: If the stressor is controllable (vacuum, visitor): remove it; if not (storm, fireworks): mitigate (den, blinds, background noise); if signs escalate (self-injury, escape attempts): alert the owner; no medication unless owner-directed.
success: Dog's stress level falls below threshold within N minutes; the intervention matches the cause; no forced contact and no medication; the owner alerted if signs escalate.
wrong: Keeps vacuuming while trying to soothe the dog
Drags the hiding dog out
Gives a sedative from the cabinet
fidelity: S: pet stress model and intervention effects
notes: Related appendix entry X-b4cc1a54265e33-01 (pets beyond feeding and walking).

text: “The dog’s limping.” Requires noticing and reporting without guessing at medical treatment.
interpretation: The dog shows a limp (hidden cause: a burr in the paw, a nail problem, a sprain, or unknown); the robot must notice it from gait asymmetry, observe which leg, since when and any other signs (paw licking, swelling, pain on rising), keep the dog from strenuous activity, and report specifics to the owner without diagnosing or treating (no medication, no manipulating the joint).
success: Report reaches the owner within the time limit naming the affected leg, onset time and observed signs; no treatment attempted; the dog rested (no walk or play).
wrong: Gives the dog human painkillers
Tells the owner 'it's probably a sprain' as a diagnosis
Takes the dog on its usual walk
notes: Related 'Report unusual pet behavior rather than guessing at medical treatment.' (Pet care, T-dda4e199f3f5b0-01).
